o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish قُنكشٖی (qoñşı), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kon- (“neighbour; friend; guest”), whence also Azerbaijani qonaq (“guest”). Compare Turkish komşu, Uzbek qoʻshni, Turkmen goňşy, Kyrgyz кошуна (koşuna, “guest”), Kumyk хоншу (xonşu).
From məqsəd (“purpose”) + yön (“direction”) + -lü. Calque of Russian целенапра́вленный (celenaprávlennyj).
